name: How does painting a foreclosed property differ from standard interior painting?

mainEntity.name: How does painting a foreclosed property differ from standard interior painting?

acceptedAnswer.text: Painting a foreclosed home requires substantially more surface preparation than standard repainting. Foreclosures frequently sit vacant and unconditioned, leading to peeling paint, water staining, drywall gouges, and stubborn odors from smoke or pets. Before any color goes on the wall, the crew must complete extensive drywall repairs, scrape loose layers, wash dirty surfaces, and apply specialized stain-blocking or odor-sealing primers. Regular interior painting projects generally involve clean walls that only need light patching and standard priming. Because HH Remodeling handles both drywall repair and interior painting directly, structural surface defects are corrected seamlessly before painting begins.
acceptedAnswer.description: Foreclosure painting requires heavy surface prep, including deep stain-blocking primers, odor remediation, and extensive drywall patching before any finish paint can be applied.
